profiles.Summary: Hearts of Iron IV is a CPU-bound grand strategy game from 2016 with modest GPU requirements, running well on the Steam Deck via Proton at platinum tier. The game's main performance challenge is late-game simulation load on the CPU rather than GPU rendering, and the interface benefits from touchscreen or trackpad use since it was designed for mouse and keyboard.

profiles.Summary: Hearts of Iron IV runs on the Steam Deck with a Platinum ProtonDB rating, meaning it generally launches and plays without major intervention, though some users have reported difficulty getting it to run smoothly enough for comfortable play. As a CPU-bound grand strategy title with a relatively simple 2D map renderer, it is not GPU-intensive but can stress the Deck's CPU in late-game with large save files, making frame pacing the primary challenge rather than raw graphical power.

MaxBattery.Notes: HOI4 is primarily CPU-bound so a low GPU clock and TDP are effective here; the 30 fps cap with a 45 Hz refresh rate gives smooth frame pacing via the Deck's 2:3 reprojection. Late-game slowdown is driven by CPU AI load, not GPU, so battery savings are maximised by keeping GPU clocks very low.

KnownIssues: Late-game (post-1942) large saves can cause significant CPU slowdown and frame drops as AI calculations increase
The UI and text can be very small on the 1280x800 screen, making it hard to read without zooming in
Steam Deck may default to running the game through Proton even though a native Linux build exists; manually selecting the native build or a specific Proton version may be needed
Some users report the game is difficult to play comfortably on Deck due to UI/UX scaling and input challenges with the complex interface

MaxPerformance.Notes: With no TDP or GPU clock limit the Deck can sustain 60 fps through most of the early and mid game where the map and AI load are manageable; expect dips in late-game mega-campaigns as the CPU becomes the bottleneck regardless of GPU headroom. This profile trades battery life for the smoothest possible early-war experience.
